rootCauses: ROOT CAUSE (single, shared): `visibleClipMediaIDs` scopes the CLIPS but never the OVERLAYS. Clips are filtered through `StudioGeometry.filterByMedia` (StudioGeometry.swift:22-25, keyed on `TimelineClip.sessionMediaID`), but EVERY overlay accessor returns the whole project array: `overlays` (StudioEditorViewModel.swift:157 `snapshot.overlays`), `canvasOverlays` (:162 `renderedOverlays(snapshot.overlays)`), `timelineOverlays` (:668 `overlays`), and `scopedSnapshot.overlays` (:150 `renderedOverlays(s.overlays)` over the FULL set even though :149 scopes `s.clips`). So a `.climbName` tag owned by a NOT-visible clip still reaches the canvas, the overlay-timeline lane, AND the export.

KEY-TYPE MISMATCH that makes scoping non-trivial: `OverlayItem.clipID` is a `TimelineClip.id` (StudioProject.swift:197-203), but `visibleClipMediaIDs` is a Set<`SessionMedia.id`> (StudioEditorViewModel.swift:25; presentStudio passes `[clip.id]` where clip is a SessionMedia, FreeformPlayerView.swift:1402). `filterByMedia` matches `sessionMediaID`, and OverlayItem has no `sessionMediaID`. Correct scoping needs the chain clipID -> owning TimelineClip -> its `sessionMediaID` -> membership in `visibleClipMediaIDs` (equivalently: clipID in the set of visible TimelineClip ids). filterByMedia CANNOT be reused directly for overlays.

WHY SYMPTOM #2 (two overlay tracks over one clip) is UNCONDITIONAL in the timeline lane: StudioTimelineView.swift:80 `ForEach(vm.timelineOverlays)` has NO time-gate and NO clip filter — it draws one OverlayBar per overlay in the full set, so a neighbour clip's tag ALWAYS shows as a second bar.

WHY the foreign tag also leaks onto the CANVAS and EXPORT (and why it overlaps in time): `outputWindow(for:)` (StudioEditorViewModel.swift:195-201) resolves a clip-bound overlay's window from `placedClips`, which is built only from `visibleSnapshotClips` (:179-182). A foreign overlay's clip is not in `placedClips`, so it FALLS BACK to its stored `[startSec,endSec]` (:200), seeded by addClimbNameOverlay as ~`[0, clipDur]` (:519-522). Single-clip compositions also start at 0 (StudioGeometry timeline cursor), so `[0,clipDurA]` overlaps the visible clip's `[0,2]`, passing both the canvas time-gate (StudioOverlayCanvas.swift:47-53) and the export time-gate (StudioOverlays.swift:41/applyVisibility). Composer reads `snapshot.overlays` directly (StudioComposer.swift:82,87) from the unfiltered `scopedSnapshot`, so the foreign tag BURNS INTO the exported single-clip file.

SYMPTOM #1 ('default climb tag — e.g. Attempt# ON — always shows up even though I set it once') is NOT a persistence/default bug — it is the SAME leak wearing a different hat. Confirmed: `showsAttempt`/`showsSetter` default OFF (`...Raw ?? false`, StudioProject.swift:281-288); `addClimbNameOverlay` is idempotent (early-return select, StudioEditorViewModel.swift:503-506) and has a SINGLE call site — the user-tapped Climb button (StudioEditorView.swift:272); `.task`/onAppear only calls `vm.select(clip.id)`, never adds an overlay; flags persist and reload via the @Model. So NOTHING auto-adds a default tag. The 'default-looking tag that always shows' is a DIFFERENT clip's persisted tag leaking through the unscoped canvas/lane; its flags reflect that other clip, which reads as 'my setting didn't stick.' Scoping overlays resolves it as a side effect (re-test required).

bugs.title: Overlay-timeline lane shows another clip's climb tag (two bars over one clip) — `timelineOverlays` is never scoped
bugs.rootCause: StudioTimelineView.swift:80 `ForEach(vm.timelineOverlays)` renders one bar per overlay with no clip filter and no time-gate; `timelineOverlays` (StudioEditorViewModel.swift:668) returns `overlays` (:157 = full `snapshot.overlays`). visibleClipMediaIDs scopes clips (filterByMedia, StudioGeometry.swift:22-25) but there is no overlay analogue. This is the user-visible 'two The cool dyn… tracks' symptom and it is unconditional (no time-gate to hide it).
bugs.fix: Route `timelineOverlays` through a new `scopedOverlays`/`visibleOverlays` helper (see fixPlan) that keeps an overlay iff (visibleClipMediaIDs==nil) OR (clipID==nil) OR (its owning clip is in the visible set). Change StudioEditorViewModel.swift:668 to `var timelineOverlays: [OverlayItem] { scopedOverlays }`.

bugs.title: Single-clip CANVAS shows another clip's climb tag — `canvasOverlays` is never scoped (only time-gated)
bugs.rootCause: StudioEditorView.swift:165 feeds `vm.canvasOverlays` to StudioOverlayCanvas; `canvasOverlays` (StudioEditorViewModel.swift:162) is `renderedOverlays(snapshot.overlays)` — the FULL set. The canvas only time-gates (StudioOverlayCanvas.swift:47-53). A foreign overlay reaches the canvas, and because its clip isn't in `placedClips`, `outputWindow(for:)` (:195-201) falls back to the stored ~[0,clipDur] window, which overlaps the visible clip's [0,2] and passes the gate.
bugs.fix: Change StudioEditorViewModel.swift:162 to `var canvasOverlays: [OverlayItem] { renderedOverlays(scopedOverlays) }`. Scope BEFORE `renderedOverlays` so foreign overlays never reach `outputWindow`.

bugs.title: Single-clip EXPORT burns in another clip's climb tag — `scopedSnapshot` scopes clips but not overlays
bugs.rootCause: `scopedSnapshot` (StudioEditorViewModel.swift:147-152) sets `s.clips = visibleSnapshotClips` (only inside `if visibleClipMediaIDs != nil`, :149) but `s.overlays = renderedOverlays(s.overlays)` (:150) runs over the FULL overlays. `renderedOverlays` (:231-241) only drops empty-content tags and re-derives windows; it never drops off-scope clipIDs. export() (:1033) and the composer (StudioComposer.swift:82,87 read `snapshot.overlays` directly; StudioOverlays.swift:41 gates only by content+time) emit the foreign tag into the file.
bugs.fix: Change StudioEditorViewModel.swift:150 to `s.overlays = renderedOverlays(scopedOverlays)`. Because `scopedOverlays` returns all overlays when visibleClipMediaIDs==nil, this is safe for the unscoped whole-workout export too (no need to guard it under the `if`).

bugs.title: Symptom #1: 'default climb tag (Attempt# ON) always shows even though I set it once' is the same cross-scope leak, not a persistence/default reset
bugs.rootCause: No code auto-adds or force-enables a tag. `showsAttempt`/`showsSetter` default OFF (StudioProject.swift:281-288); `addClimbNameOverlay` is idempotent (StudioEditorViewModel.swift:503-506) with a single user-tap call site (StudioEditorView.swift:272); onAppear/.task only calls `vm.select(clip.id)`; flags persist+reload. The tag the user sees in the single-clip editor is a DIFFERENT clip's tag (the next attempt's) leaking via the unscoped canvas/lane, carrying that clip's flags — which looks like 'my setting was lost / a default came back.'
bugs.fix: No persistence/default change — do NOT 'fix' the toggles or add a reset (that would be a misdiagnosis). Apply the overlay-scoping fix; the single-clip editor will then show only the focused clip's own persisted tag. THEN re-test symptom #1 on a truly single isolated clip+tag. If 'Attempt# ON' STILL reproduces, audit select(_:) (StudioEditorViewModel.swift:364-375) + refreshAttemptLineForSelection (:595-601) for an unexpected showsAttempt flip — but current evidence says it will resolve.

bugs.title: Selection can still target a now-hidden (foreign) overlay after scoping
bugs.rootCause: `selectedOverlay` (StudioEditorViewModel.swift:158) and the style/Attempt/Setter panel act on `selectedOverlayID` resolved against the full `overlays`. select(_:) (:364-375) repoints to `climbOverlayForSelectedClip` (this clip's tag), so in normal flow the selection is in-scope. But if `selectedOverlayID` ever points at an off-scope tag, the control panel could edit a tag the canvas no longer shows.
bugs.fix: Low priority / belt-and-suspenders. After scoping, optionally clear or repoint `selectedOverlayID` when it falls outside `scopedOverlays` (e.g. in the onAppear focus step or a didSet). Keep selection ACCESSORS (`selectedOverlay`, `climbOverlayForSelectedClip` :487-490) reading the full `overlays` so a scoped EDIT still persists to the shared project — only the RENDER lists (canvas/lane/export) get scoped.

fixPlan: STEP 1 (the helper, lowest risk, unblocks everything): Add `overlayInScope(_:)` + `scopedOverlays` to StudioEditorViewModel.swift (exact code in sharedHelperNeeded). Semantics: nil scope -> all; clipID==nil -> keep (whole-project overlay shows in every scope, matching StudioProject.swift:200-202); else resolve clipID -> owning clip's sessionMediaID -> test membership in visibleClipMediaIDs; clip gone / no sessionMediaID -> hide. Resolve against `snapshot.clips` (full), not the scoped list.

STEP 2 (CANVAS): StudioEditorViewModel.swift:162 -> `var canvasOverlays: [OverlayItem] { renderedOverlays(scopedOverlays) }`. Scope BEFORE renderedOverlays so foreign overlays never reach outputWindow's stale-window fallback. (Fixes symptom #2 on the canvas and the conditional canvas leak.)
STEP 3 (TIMELINE LANE): StudioEditorViewModel.swift:668 -> `var timelineOverlays: [OverlayItem] { scopedOverlays }`. (Fixes the unconditional two-bars symptom in StudioTimelineView.swift:80.)

STEP 4 (EXPORT/PREVIEW): StudioEditorViewModel.swift:150 -> `s.overlays = renderedOverlays(scopedOverlays)`. Safe to leave OUTSIDE the `if visibleClipMediaIDs != nil` guard because scopedOverlays returns all overlays when scope is nil; this single change corrects both export() (:1033) and rebuildPreview, which both consume scopedSnapshot. (Fixes the burn-in.)

STEP 5 (do NOT touch the edit/selection path): leave `overlays` (:157), `selectedOverlay` (:158), and `climbOverlayForSelectedClip` (:487-490) reading the FULL `snapshot.overlays`, so a scoped edit still persists to the shared project (the documented cross-scope-persistence invariant) and add-or-select stays idempotent. `hasPiP` (:952) and the kind lookups (:647,658,673,989) inherit no behavior change since they only receive in-scope ids. Do NOT add a default tag, reset toggles, or change showsAttempt/showsSetter defaults — symptom #1 is the leak, not a default.

STEP 6 (guard rail): add a pure unit test (ideally extract `StudioGeometry.filterOverlays(_:visibleClipIDs:)` for device-free XCTest): 2 clips, one climb tag each; scope=[mediaA] => canvasOverlays and timelineOverlays contain ONLY clipA's tag (plus any clipID==nil overlay). Optionally a debug assert in outputWindow when a clip-bound overlay can't resolve its clip while scoping is active, to catch future regressions.

STEP 7 (re-verify symptom #1 explicitly): after STEPS 1-4, open a single isolated climb clip with its own tag and confirm it shows exactly ONE tag with the user's persisted Attempt#/setter state. If 'Attempt# default ON' STILL reproduces on a truly single tag, that is a SEPARATE bug — audit select(_:) (:364-375) and refreshAttemptLineForSelection (:595-601) for an unexpected showsAttempt flip; current evidence indicates it will be resolved by scoping.
STEP 8 (optional, low): clear/repoint selectedOverlayID when it falls outside scopedOverlays (onAppear focus step or didSet) so the style/Attempt/Setter panel can never edit an off-scope tag.
